info.title: Scrutari Post-Quantum Gateway — Public REST API
info.description:
Programmatic interface for managing routes, tenants, domains, members, and API keys.

Authentication is via API keys minted from the dashboard or via the admin CLI; pass them as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

Every non-2xx response returns the same `ApiError` envelope (see `components/schemas/ApiError`). List endpoints return a `Page<T>` envelope with `data`, `has_more`, and an optional `next_cursor`.

This is an alpha-tagged spec. The shape is stable, but new endpoints will land additively as more `/v1/*` surfaces gain `#[utoipa::path]` annotations.

get.summary:
List the caller's API keys. Returns a paginated
`Page<ApiKeyResponse>` envelope; the response shape is the
**masked** form — `plaintext` is NEVER included in a list
response, only at the original `POST /v1/api_keys` mint call.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit on the first page.

200.description: Paginated list of active API keys for the authenticated tenant. Revoked keys are filtered out.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

post.summary:
Mint a new API key. **The plaintext secret is included in the
response and is shown ONLY on this call** — there is no recovery
path. The dashboard / CLI must display it immediately and let
the operator store it before navigating away.
post.description:
Subsequent reads of this key via `GET /v1/api_keys` return
`ApiKeyResponse` (metadata + `key_hint` only, no plaintext).

Common failure modes:

- **`422 name_invalid`** — name is empty or longer than 100 chars.
- **`422 scope_invalid`** — at least one scope isn't in the
  accepted vocabulary. See [`CreateApiKeyRequest::scopes`] for
  the list, or fetch the dynamic registry at `GET /v1/scopes`
  (planned) once it lands.
- **`422 environment_invalid`** — environment is set to something
  other than `live` or `test`.

requestBody.description: Key parameters. `tenant_id` is derived from the authenticated caller, not the body.

200.description: Key minted. **The `plaintext` field carries the secret and is visible exactly once** — store it before navigating away. Subsequent reads return `ApiKeyResponse` without the plaintext.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

delete.summary:
Revoke an API key. The row stays in storage (marked
`revoked_at`) so auth-failure audit logs still resolve the
`api_key_id` to a human-readable label — "delete" at the API
level is "revoke" at the data model.
delete.description:
Subsequent presentations of the revoked key by an attacker
return `401` from the auth middleware. Lost keys can be safely
revoked AND should be: there is no way to recover the
plaintext, and a revoked key cannot be re-enabled (mint a new
one instead).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Key identifier, prefix `ak_` followed by base32-no-pad.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

404.description: No active key with this id for the authenticated tenant.

422.description: Path parameter `id` doesn't match the `ak_*` format.

get.summary:
List domain verifications for the authenticated tenant. Returns
a paginated `Page<DomainResponse>` envelope.
get.description:
The list includes domains in every state — `pending`,
`verified`, `failed`, `expired` — so a Terraform provider's
`data "scrutari_domain"` can present accurate state. To filter
to only verified domains, the caller filters client-side
(a `?status=` query parameter is planned but not yet landed).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit on the first page.

200.description: Paginated list of domain verifications for the authenticated tenant.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

get.summary:
Fetch a single domain verification by id. Returns 404 for
domains that don't exist OR exist for a different tenant — same
anti-disclosure posture as other tenant-scoped reads.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Domain verification identifier from a previous list response.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

404.description: No domain verification with this id exists for the authenticated tenant.

422.description: Path parameter `id` is not a positive integer.

get.summary:
List members of the authenticated tenant. Returns a paginated
`Page<MemberResponse>` envelope. Deactivated members are
filtered out at the data layer; the response contains only
active members.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit on the first page.

200.description: Paginated list of active tenant members.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

get.summary:
Fetch a single tenant member by `user_id` (UUID). Returns 404 for
users that don't exist in this tenant — same anti-disclosure
posture as other tenant-scoped reads.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Member identifier as a UUID v4 in canonical hyphenated form.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

404.description: No member with this user_id exists in the authenticated tenant.

422.description: Path parameter `user_id` is not a valid UUID.

get.summary:
List routes for the authenticated tenant. Returns a paginated
`Page<RouteResponse>` envelope. Pass the response's `next_cursor`
as the `?cursor=` query parameter to fetch the next page.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque pagination cursor from the previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit on the first page.

200.description: Paginated list of routes for the authenticated tenant.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

post.summary:
Create a new route. Returns the newly-created `RouteResponse`
with its server-assigned `id`.
post.description:
Common failure modes worth noting in client code:

- **`409 route_conflict`** — another route on this host already
  uses the same `path_prefix`. The conflict is checked globally
  (across tenants) but the response does not reveal the owning
  tenant.
- **`422 plan_limit_reached`** — the tenant's plan caps the
  number of routes and that cap is hit. Upgrade or delete an
  existing route first.
- **`403 domain_not_verified`** — `host` is not a verified
  domain for this tenant. Verify via the operator-tier
  `POST /admin/domains` flow first.

requestBody.description: Route to create. `tenant_id` is derived from the API key and must NOT be specified in the body.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

403.description: API key lacks the `routes:write` scope, or `host` is not a verified domain for this tenant.

409.description: Another route already matches `(host, path_prefix)`. PATCH the existing route or DELETE it before recreating.

422.description: Validation failure — invalid `auth_mode`, malformed `path_prefix` / `upstream_url`, or plan-cap reached.

get.summary:
Fetch a single route by id. Returns 404 for routes that don't
exist OR exist for a different tenant — the two cases are
intentionally indistinguishable to foreclose existence-disclosure.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Route identifier returned from a previous create or list call.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

404.description: No route with this id exists for the authenticated tenant.

422.description: Path parameter `id` is not a positive integer.

delete.summary: Delete a route. Returns 204 No Content on success.
delete.description:
The deletion is hard, not soft: the `(host, path_prefix)` slot
becomes immediately available for another route. If you need
to temporarily cut traffic, prefer `PATCH /v1/routes/{id}`
with `{"is_active": false}` — same effect, reversible without
re-creation.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

404.description: No route with this id exists for the authenticated tenant.

422.description: Path parameter `id` is not a positive integer.

patch.summary:
Partial update — every field in the body is optional; omitted =
unchanged. `host` and `tenant_id` are intentionally NOT
patchable: re-homing a route to a new host is delete-then-create.
patch.description:
Common failure modes:

- **`404 route_not_found`** — id doesn't exist OR exists for a
  different tenant.
- **`409 route_conflict`** — the requested `path_prefix` would
  collide with another route on the same host.

requestBody.description: Partial update. Omit any field you don't want to change.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

404.description: No route with this id exists for the authenticated tenant.

409.description: Requested `path_prefix` collides with another route on the same host.

422.description: Validation failure on a body field or path parameter.

get.summary: List tenants accessible to the caller.
get.description:
The authenticated API key is scoped to exactly one tenant, so this
endpoint always returns at most one row — surfaced as a
`Page<TenantResponse>` envelope (with `has_more: false` and no
cursor) for client-SDK consistency with the multi-row list
endpoints. Iterate it like any other list and you'll get the
caller's own tenant.

200.description: List of tenants accessible to the caller. Always exactly one row — the tenant the API key is scoped to. Returned as a `Page` envelope (with `has_more: false`, no cursor) for client-SDK consistency with the multi-row list endpoints.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

403.description: API key is valid but lacks the `tenants:read` scope.

500.description: Internal error. Includes a `request_id` clients should quote when contacting support.

get.summary:
Subscribe to the per-tenant live trace stream. Long-lived
`text/event-stream` response delivering one event per request /
handshake / data-plane signal observed at the gateway.
get.description:
# Wire format

Standard W3C Server-Sent Events. Each event carries:

- **`id:`** — opaque resume cursor (a Redis Stream message ID,
  e.g. `1715126400123-0`). Clients reconnecting after a network
  blip should send the last-seen value as the
  `Last-Event-ID` request header to resume without gaps or
  replay.
- **`data:`** — a single-line JSON object describing the event
  (see the data-shape section below).

Empty SSE comment frames (`: keepalive`) fire every 15 seconds
to prevent intermediate proxies (nginx, Azure Front Door, AWS
ALB) from timing out idle connections. Clients should ignore
them.

# Connection model

One connection per dashboard tab is the typical deployment
shape. The browser's `EventSource` API does automatic reconnect
with backoff; custom clients (curl, Go, Python `requests` with
`stream=True`) should implement equivalent reconnect-with-
`Last-Event-ID` semantics. A per-tenant connection cap is on the
roadmap (followup #195) but not enforced today.

# Data shape

Each `data:` line is a JSON object with this minimal common shape:

```json
{
  "at": "2026-05-07T13:00:00.123Z",
  "trace_id": "01k4r9j7y8x2v3m6q1w5z9b7n2",
  "kind": { ... }
}
```

`kind` is a tagged discriminated union — the `"type"` discriminant
names the event variant (`request_started`, `request_completed`,
`handshake_completed`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, etc.) and the
remaining fields carry the variant-specific payload.

**The schema-typed model of `kind` is intentionally NOT in this
OpenAPI spec.** The trace event is a complex Rust enum
(`shared_kernel::tracing::TraceEvent`) that mirrors data-plane
internals; encoding its full structure in OpenAPI would couple the
public spec to internal representation churn. We document the
data shape in prose here; the canonical reference for variant
names and payload fields is
<https://docs.scrutari.ai/v1/traces/event-types> (live with the
trace-event guide; deferred to followup #230 if/when we promote
the type to a public-facing schema).

# Authentication and tenancy

Requires the `traces:read` scope on the presented API key. The
stream is tenant-scoped from the authenticated key, NEVER from
any query parameter — cross-tenant event leakage is structurally
impossible at this layer.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Opaque resume cursor from the most recent `id:` field a previous connection received. Send on reconnect to resume the stream from that point without gaps or replay. Omit on the first connection to receive only events arriving AFTER the connection opens (no historical replay).

200.description: Subscription opened. Response body is a `text/event-stream` of `id:` + `data:` frames, one per event, plus periodic `: keepalive` comments. The connection stays open indefinitely; close the underlying TCP/TLS connection to unsubscribe. See the endpoint description for the JSON shape of the `data:` field.

401.description: Missing, malformed, or revoked API key.

500.description: Internal error — typically the trace backend (Redis) is unreachable. Retry with backoff; the `EventSource` API does this automatically.

ApiError.description:
The wire shape of an error response. Matches the OpenAPI spec
exactly. `#[serde(rename = "error")]` ensures the JSON body is
`{ "error": { ... } }`, not `{ ... }`, so clients can do
`response.error.code` cleanly.

ApiErrorBody.description: Inner error object — the actual payload clients destructure.

ApiKeyResponse.description:
Safe-to-read wire shape for an API key. Returned by every
surface except the one-shot `POST /v1/api_keys` creation
(which uses [`IssuedApiKeyResponse`]).

Carries metadata + `key_hint` (last 4 chars for display).
Does NOT carry the plaintext or the Argon2id hash; those are
not recoverable from a list/read response.

key_hint.description: Last 4 characters of the secret body.

last_used_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent use.
`null` for keys that have never been presented to the
auth middleware. Updated asynchronously (the gateway
batches `last_used_at` writes to limit row contention on
hot keys).

name.description:
Human-readable label for this key. Surfaced in the
dashboard's API Keys table; useful for distinguishing
keys by purpose ("terraform-prod", "ci-runner",
"vendor-X-integration"). 1-100 characters.

scopes.description:
Capability scopes the key grants. Each scope is a
`<resource>:<action>` pair. Server validates against a
closed list; unknown scopes return `422 scope_invalid`.

Current valid values: `*` (wildcard, all scopes),
`api_keys:read`, `api_keys:write`, `routes:read`,
`routes:write`, `domains:read`, `domains:write`,
`members:read`, `members:write`, `tenants:read`,
`tenants:write`, `audit_log:read`, `traces:read`.

The Terraform provider should query the dynamic
`GET /v1/scopes` registry (planned) rather than hardcoding
this list, so new scopes flow in without a provider
release.

environment.description:
Optional environment selector. `live` (default) issues a
production key; `test` issues a sandbox key. Test keys
route to a separate environment with no real billing —
suitable for CI smoke tests and dev workflows.

CreateRouteRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /v1/routes`.

`tenant_id` is intentionally NOT a body field — it's derived
from the authenticated API key, not taken from the request, to
foreclose the "specify someone else's tenant in the body" class
of cross-tenant attack.

host.description:
Host the route matches. Must be a verified domain for the
caller's tenant (see `POST /admin/domains` to verify a new
domain). Lower-cased on the server before storage; case is
not significant on match.

path_prefix.description:
URL path prefix to match. Must start with `/`. The pair
`(host, path_prefix)` is globally unique across all
tenants; conflicts return `409 route_conflict` (without
disclosing the owning tenant).

upstream_url.description:
Where to forward matched traffic. Must be `http://...` or
`https://...`. The gateway validates the scheme; the host
itself is NOT validated at create time (it might not yet
resolve; that's a deploy-time concern, not a create-time
concern).

preserve_host_header.description:
Forward the client's `Host:` header unchanged. Default
false.

auth_mode.description:
Authentication mode. One of `required` (default), `optional`,
`passthrough`. Opening a route to anonymous traffic should
always be an explicit choice, hence the safe default.

DomainResponse.description:
Public response shape for a single domain verification.

Mirrors the storage row (`repo::DomainVerification`) minus the
`expected_value` secret — see the module docs for why.

id.description:
Auto-assigned verification identifier. Stable for the
lifetime of the row; not reused after deletion.

tenant_id.description:
Owning tenant. Read-only — derived from the authenticated
caller.

domain.description:
The customer-supplied domain name being verified. Stored
as the case-folded form the gateway uses for matching.

verification_type.description:
Verification method. Today: `dns_txt` (TXT record check)
or `cname` (CNAME chain check). Stored as a string rather
than a wire enum so future methods (DNS-01 wildcard,
HTTP-01 file challenge) can be added without bumping the
API major version.

challenge_host.description:
The hostname the gateway queries when running the proof.
For `dns_txt` this is typically `_scrutari-verify.<domain>`;
for `cname` it's the `<domain>` itself. The dashboard's
verification UI surfaces this so customers know which
record to inspect when troubleshooting.

status.description:
Current verification state. One of:

  - `pending`  — challenge issued, no successful check yet.
  - `verified` — the gateway has confirmed control.
  - `failed`   — exceeded max attempts; reset via
    `/admin/domains` (the public API can't reset).
  - `expired`  — past `expires_at`; the row stays for audit
    but no longer counts as proof of control.

attempts.description:
Count of verification attempts the gateway has run for
this row. Increments on every `dns_txt`/`cname` lookup.
Used by the rate-limiter to back off after repeated
failures.

last_error.description:
Last DNS-level error encountered, or null if no error.
Surfaced verbatim to the dashboard so customers can
distinguish "record not found" (likely TTL not propagated)
from "record present but wrong value" (likely copy-paste
mistake).

created_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of when the verification row
was created (= when the challenge was issued).

updated_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent verification
attempt or state change.

verified_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of successful verification, or
null if the row has not been verified yet (or has since
expired).

expires_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp after which this verification
row no longer counts as proof of control. The dashboard
prompts re-verification before this point; expired rows
remain readable for audit.

ErrorType.description:
Coarse error categorization. Stable enum: variants will not be
removed within a major version. Clients switch on this for retry
and surfacing logic.

HTTP status code mapping is fixed and exposed via
[`ErrorType::status_code`] (returns a `u16` to avoid pulling axum
or http types into the no-default-features dep graph).

IssuedApiKeyResponse.description:
`POST /v1/api_keys` response — the ONLY shape in the public
API that carries a plaintext secret. The dashboard or CLI MUST
display `plaintext` to the user immediately; subsequent reads
of the same key (via `GET /v1/api_keys`) return
[`ApiKeyResponse`] without `plaintext`. There is no recovery
path — lost keys must be revoked and re-issued.

Security review notes for anyone touching this type:

  * Adding a new field that contains secret material (e.g. a
    refresh token, a webhook signing key) is a wire-contract
    change AND a security-classification change. Both need
    explicit security-review sign-off.
  * NEVER add `plaintext` (or any equivalent secret field) to
    `ApiKeyResponse`. That type is the "safe to read on every
    subsequent call" surface; widening it would defeat the
    entire mint-once design.

id.description:
Key identifier. Prefix `ak_` followed by base32-no-pad.
Stable across the key's lifetime; survives revocation
(the row is marked `revoked_at`, not deleted).

tenant_id.description:
Owning tenant. Read-only — derived from the authenticated
caller, never specified in the request body.

name.description: Operator-supplied label, echoed from the request.

scopes.description: Granted scopes, echoed from the request.

environment.description:
`live` or `test`. Defaults to `live` if the request
omitted the field.

key_hint.description:
Last 4 characters of the secret body, for display. Useful
for "the key ending in `XyZ9`" UI when the customer has
many keys.

plaintext.description:
**One-time-only plaintext secret.** Format
`scru_(live|test)_<26-chars>`. The dashboard / CLI MUST
surface this once and never store it. Lost keys cannot be
recovered — revoke + re-issue.

This field is on the `IssuedApiKeyResponse` type
EXCLUSIVELY; the list/read shape
([`ApiKeyResponse`]) does NOT carry it.

MemberResponse.description:
Public response shape for a single tenant member.

Returns the minimum-viable shape any membership-management UI
needs: identity, role, contact, timestamps. Does NOT include
internal fields like `last_session_at` (operational telemetry,
dashboard-only) or `password_hash` (irrelevant in the OIDC-only
auth model; not stored in our table).

user_id.description:
Stable identifier for the user across tenants. UUID v4
generated at first sign-in (or at invitation accept).
Hyphenated canonical form on the wire.

tenant_id.description:
Owning tenant. Read-only — derived from the authenticated
caller.

role.description:
Role assignment. Stored as a string rather than a wire
enum so role names can evolve additively. Current values:

  - `owner`  — full administrative access; can mint
    billing-impacting changes.
  - `admin`  — full operational access; no billing-tier
    decisions.
  - `member` — read+write on routes/domains; no
    member-management or billing.
  - `viewer` — read-only across the tenant.

Role assignment changes through `/admin/members`; this
public surface is read-only.

email.description:
Email of record for this member. Used by the dashboard's
invitation flow, by audit-log row attribution, and by the
password-recovery email path (when applicable to the
tenant's auth mode).

PII — see the module-level docs for handling guidance.

display_name.description:
Human-readable name. Falls back to the email if the
identity provider didn't supply a display name at
sign-in (rare; most IdPs supply one).

created_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of when this user first
joined the tenant (invitation accept, JIT provision, or
founder-claim).

updated_at.description:
ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 timestamp of the most recent change
to this row (role change, display-name update, etc.).

PageApiKeyResponse.description:
Concrete paginated envelope for the wire shape
. Generated by the `concrete_page!` macro — see the
module docs for the rationale on non-generic page
types.

PageDomainResponse.description:
Concrete paginated envelope for the wire shape
. Generated by the `concrete_page!` macro — see the
module docs for the rationale on non-generic page
types.

PageMemberResponse.description:
Concrete paginated envelope for the wire shape
. Generated by the `concrete_page!` macro — see the
module docs for the rationale on non-generic page
types.

PageRouteResponse.description:
Concrete paginated envelope for the wire shape
. Generated by the `concrete_page!` macro — see the
module docs for the rationale on non-generic page
types.

PageTenantResponse.description:
Concrete paginated envelope for the wire shape
. Generated by the `concrete_page!` macro — see the
module docs for the rationale on non-generic page
types.

RevokeApiKeyResponse.description:
`DELETE /v1/api_keys/{id}` response. Returned with 200 OK on
successful revocation. The key row stays in storage (marked
`revoked_at`) so auth-failure audit logs still resolve
`api_key_id` to a human-readable label after revocation;
"delete" at the API level is "revoke" at the data model.

id.description: Identifier of the key that was revoked.

revoked.description:
Always `true` for a successful response — included
explicitly so clients that match on the field rather than
the HTTP status get a clear signal.

RouteResponse.description:
Wire response for a single route.

Returned by:
  - `GET    /v1/routes`         (inside `Page<RouteResponse>.data[]`)
  - `GET    /v1/routes/{id}`
  - `POST   /v1/routes`         (201 Created)
  - `PATCH  /v1/routes/{id}`

`DELETE /v1/routes/{id}` returns 204 with no body.

id.description:
Auto-assigned route identifier. Stable for the lifetime of
the row; not reused after deletion. Use in subsequent
`/v1/routes/{id}` calls.

tenant_id.description:
Owning tenant. Read-only — the gateway populates this from
the authenticated API key on create. Cannot be specified or
changed via the public API.

host.description:
Host header / SNI the route matches against. The host must
be verified for this tenant via `POST /admin/domains` before
a route can be created; unverified hosts return
`403 domain_not_verified` from POST.

path_prefix.description:
URL path prefix the route matches. Must start with `/`.
Combined with `host` to form the (host, path_prefix) match
key — duplicates across tenants return `409 route_conflict`.

upstream_url.description:
Where to forward matched traffic. Must be `http://...` or
`https://...` with a non-empty host. The gateway terminates
inbound PQ-TLS and re-establishes outbound TLS (or plain
HTTP for `http://` upstreams in dev environments).

strip_path_prefix.description:
If true, strip `path_prefix` from the request path before
forwarding. Example: matching `/orders` and forwarding to
`https://upstream/` rewrites `GET /orders/123` upstream to
`GET /123`.

preserve_host_header.description:
If true, forward the client's `Host:` header unchanged.
Default false; the gateway substitutes the upstream host
derived from `upstream_url`. Set true when the upstream's
virtual-host routing depends on the original host header.

is_active.description:
When false, the route is administratively disabled — the
gateway returns 503 for matching requests instead of
forwarding. Useful for incident response (cut a route
without deleting it) and for staged rollouts.

auth_mode.description:
Authentication mode for traffic on this route:

  - `required` — every request must present a valid API key
    (or other configured auth). Default; safest posture.
  - `optional` — auth is checked when present (and forwarded
    to the upstream via X-Scrutari-* headers) but missing
    auth doesn't reject. Use for routes that need to serve
    anonymous and authenticated traffic with the same
    handler.
  - `passthrough` — auth is not checked at all. Use for
    truly public surfaces (marketing pages, health checks).

updated_at.description:
Last-modified timestamp. Updated on every PATCH that changes
any field. RFC 3339 / ISO 8601.

TenantResponse.description:
Tenant wire response.

# Field-level OpenAPI annotations

`#[schema(example = "...")]` populates the example values in the
generated OpenAPI spec. These are operator-facing documentation
— pick values that are obviously fictional but typical-shaped
(correct length, correct prefix conventions) so a customer
reading the spec immediately understands the format.

name.description:
Display name as configured by the tenant. Customer-facing
label only; never used for routing or scoping decisions.

plan.description:
Subscription tier. Drives rate limits, plan caps, and
feature gates. One of `starter`, `growth`, `enterprise`.

rate_limit_rps.description:
Per-tenant rate-limit knobs, surfaced so the operator can
confirm what plan the gateway is enforcing without a
separate /usage call. Not editable through this surface
today.

features.description:
Free-form feature flags. Wire shape is the same JSONB object
the gateway reads internally; client SDKs treat unknown keys
as absent (false). Schema-typed as `object` since the keys
and values are inherently dynamic.

UpdateRouteRequest.description:
Request body for `PATCH /v1/routes/{id}`. Every field is
`Option`; omitted = unchanged. `host` and `tenant_id` are
intentionally NOT patchable — re-homing a route to a new host
is a delete-then-create at the API surface (same posture the
data plane takes).

upstream_url.description:
New upstream URL. Same validation as POST (`http(s)://` +
non-empty host).

auth_mode.description:
Change `auth_mode`. Must be `required` / `optional` /
`passthrough`. Lowering from `required` to `optional` or
`passthrough` opens a previously-authenticated route to
anonymous traffic — review carefully.

is_active.description:
Administrative enable/disable. When false, the route stays
in the routing table but returns 503 for matching requests.
Use for cut-without-delete during incident response.

tags.name: tenants
tags.description: Tenant resource — read the caller's own tenant row.

tags.name: routes
tags.description: Route resource — full CRUD. Primary surface managed by the Scrutari Terraform provider's `scrutari_route` resource. Routes map customer-facing `(host, path_prefix)` pairs to upstream URLs that the gateway proxies traffic to.

tags.name: api_keys
tags.description: API key resource — mint, list, revoke. **The plaintext secret is returned exactly once** in the `POST /v1/api_keys` response (`IssuedApiKeyResponse.plaintext`); subsequent reads via `GET /v1/api_keys` use the masked `ApiKeyResponse` shape that carries only metadata + `key_hint`. There is no recovery path for lost keys; revoke and re-issue.

tags.name: domains
tags.description: Domain verification resource — read-only on the public API. Domain registration and verification orchestration happen via the dashboard or the operator-tier `/admin/domains` surface; the public read endpoints exist so a Terraform `data "scrutari_domain"` data source can inspect verified-domain state without mutating it. The wire shape DELIBERATELY excludes the `expected_value` verification secret — surfacing it would let any holder of a `domains:read` key forge proofs of control.

tags.name: members
tags.description: Tenant membership resource — read-only on the public API. Identity, role, contact info, and timestamps. Adding / removing members and changing roles happen via the dashboard or `/admin/members`. PII surface — email and display_name are exposed; same disclosure as `/admin/members` so no new attack surface, but callers should handle responses with PII-appropriate care.

tags.name: traces
tags.description: Live request/handshake trace stream. The single endpoint here (`GET /v1/traces/stream`) returns a long-lived `text/event-stream` of events as the gateway processes them. Designed for dashboard observability surfaces; programmatic consumers should use `EventSource` (browser) or an equivalent SSE library and implement reconnect-with-`Last-Event-ID` for gap-free resume across network blips. The data payload shape is documented in prose on the endpoint (not yet a typed OpenAPI schema — followup #230).
